name: Snowflake

field_reviews.reason: OAuth is a first-class documented auth method for the SQL API and REST APIs and the recommended method for the Snowflake-managed MCP server ('Snowflake OAuth by default, with optional External OAuth'). Key-pair JWT and PATs are equally documented, so 'primary' is somewhat a convention call, but OAuth is defensible and the docs support it.

SQL API authentication docs (draft evidence, confirmed) list OAuth, key-pair JWT, and programmatic access tokens, all sent as Authorization: Bearer with X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type; REST API docs add workload identity federation. All draft-listed methods are real.

Correct but the draft attached no evidence URL to the access claim. Official Trial Accounts docs confirm: self-service signup form at signup.snowflake.com, only a valid email required ('no payment information or other qualifying information'), 30-day trial (or until free credits deplete), account suspended afterward unless converted to paid via credit card — matching 'self-serve trial, no permanent free tier' exactly.
SQL API executes arbitrary SQL over REST and the Snowflake REST APIs manage account objects (databases, warehouses, users, etc.) — effectively full-platform programmatic coverage.
REST (SQL API + REST APIs) confirmed in live docs; MCP via the Snowflake-managed MCP server (CREATE MCP SERVER object, standards-based interface) confirmed on the live cortex-agents-mcp docs page.

The Snowflake-managed MCP server is unambiguously first-party: documented at docs.snowflake.com, created as an in-account object, Snowflake OAuth by default, serving Cortex Analyst/Search/Agents and SQL execution as tools. Composio SNOWFLAKE toolkit listing matches the draft's citation (own-credentials auth category).

Self-service trial gives immediate account access; key-pair, PAT, and OAuth integrations are all user/admin-configurable without vendor approval — buildable today (ongoing use requires converting to paid).
No access blocker for building and testing; the trial-to-paid conversion is a cost consideration rather than a gate, consistent with sibling drafts treating self_serve_trial with null blocker.

notes: Re-fetched the SQL API authentication docs (draft evidence URL, live and matching), the Snowflake-managed MCP server page (first-party, OAuth default, Cortex + SQL execution tools — verifying the vendor MCP claim), and independently found the missing access evidence: the official Trial Accounts page documenting self-service 30-day signup with no payment info. All values stand; access moved to PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED only because the draft lacked an evidence URL for it.
